chunks: The Lord of the heavens and the earth, and all that lies between them, the Most Merciful, to whom none may dare address a word.

key_terms.الرَّحْمَٰنُ: The Most Merciful (a specific divine attribute)

ai.seo_question: Who is the Lord of the heavens and the earth according to this verse?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse underscores Allah's absolute sovereignty (Rububiyyah) over the cosmos, contrasting His eternal self-sufficiency with the impotence of idols who lack the capacity to even address Him. It serves as a theological refutation of polytheism by highlighting that creation cannot communicate with the Creator on equal footing, reinforcing the concept of Tawhid al-Uluhiyyah.
